name: Headroom
cost: Free and open source (Apache 2.0). A paid Enterprise plan exists for teams. Prices are not stated in the README
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, VS Code Copilot, Aider, OpenCode, Cline, Continue, Goose and other OpenAI-compatible or MCP clients
short: Shrinks tool outputs, logs, files and RAG chunks on your machine before they reach the model, so your coding agent sends fewer tokens.
what: Headroom compresses what your AI agent reads, including tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, files and conversation history, before it goes to the model. Compression runs locally and keeps the originals, so the model can fetch the full text when it needs it. You can use it as a Python or TypeScript library, as a local proxy, by wrapping a coding agent with one command, or as an MCP server.
who: People who run coding agents daily on long sessions with heavy tool output, especially across more than one agent. Skip it if you only use one provider's built-in compaction, mostly have short chats or prose, or work somewhere local processes can't run.
needs: Python 3.10 or newer for the CLI. The README's uv install uses Python 3.13
uv, pip or pipx to install it. The npm package is only the TypeScript library and has no `headroom` command
A coding agent or app that talks to an AI model provider
Native wheels cover macOS Apple Silicon and Linux. On an Intel Mac the README says to use the Docker install

steps.title: Install the CLI
steps.text: The README recommends uv so the command lives in its own environment. pip works too.

steps.title: Check the install
steps.text: If the command isn't found, run `uv tool update-shell` to put `~/.local/bin` on your PATH.

steps.title: Wrap your coding agent
steps.text: This starts a local proxy and launches the agent routed through Headroom. Swap `claude` for `codex`, `aider`, `opencode` and the other names in the README. Launch it this way each session.

steps.title: Or run it as a proxy
steps.text: Point any OpenAI-compatible client at it. You don't need to change any code.

steps.title: Check it works and watch the savings
steps.text: `headroom doctor` confirms routing works. The dashboard needs the proxy to be running.

steps.title: Undo it
steps.text: This removes the wrapping and the registrations it added.

try.label: From the README
try.text: After a few wrapped sessions, run `headroom savings` to see how much it saved on your own traffic.

watch: An anonymous telemetry beacon is on by default. It reports compression ratios, counters, provider and model IDs, OS and architecture, never prompts or code. Turn it off with `HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.
`headroom wrap` also installs Serena for code navigation and registers it as an MCP server in `~/.claude.json` for that project. Add `--code-memory none` to skip it.
`headroom learn` writes corrections into files like `CLAUDE.local.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` in your project.
When wrapping OpenCode with a third-party provider such as DeepSeek or OpenRouter, pass `--openai-api-url` with that provider's URL. Otherwise your key is sent to OpenAI and rejected.
Savings depend on how repetitive the content is. Prose, short chats and already-dense output compress very little.
The proxy checks PyPI for updates once a day. Set `HEADROOM_UPDATE_CHECK=off` to stop it.
The README's fix for SSL errors on corporate networks pipes the Rust installer into your shell. Read that script before running it.
